proposals.before: He Yin of the Secretariat, the empress's cousin, was kept close and set to attend in the Hall of Direct Service. Once the emperor walked behind him calling him "Three Fathers." They plotted to kill the High Ancestor and put Yin in charge; Yin would not take it, stalled and talked him down, and the plan died away.
proposals.after: He Yin of the Secretariat, the empress's paternal uncle (collateral uncle), was kept close and set to attend in the Hall of Direct Service. Once the emperor walked behind him calling him "Three Fathers." They plotted to kill the High Ancestor and put Yin in charge; Yin would not take it, stalled and talked him down, and the plan died away.
proposals.reason: 從叔 is a paternal collateral uncle, not a cousin.

decisions.reason: Chinese 小名法身 names a childhood personal name (小名), not a taboo name (諱); 'childhood taboo' is wrong, and 'childhood name' restores the correct sense.
皇太孫 is the emperor's grandson established as heir after the crown prince's death, not a great-grandson; the proposed 'imperial grandson-heir' matches 立昭業爲皇太孫.
Same unit: 皇太孫 denotes the imperial grandson-heir, not 'imperial great-grandson'; the literal repair correctly replaces the false generation term.
In 世祖崩，太孫卽位 the subject 太孫 is the same grandson-heir just established as 皇太孫, not a great-grandson; 'imperial grandson-heir' is accurate.
Literal 太孫 likewise means the imperial grandson-heir who takes the throne, not a great-grandson; the proposed replacement is correct.

decisions.after: He Yin of the Secretariat, the empress's collateral paternal uncle, was kept close and set to attend in the Hall of Direct Service. Once the emperor walked behind him calling him "Three Fathers." They plotted to kill the High Ancestor and put Yin in charge; Yin would not take it, stalled and talked him down, and the plan died away.
decisions.reason: 從叔 is a collateral paternal uncle, so 'cousin' is wrong; the proposal's sense is right, but 'paternal uncle (collateral uncle)' is redundant—use 'collateral paternal uncle'.
